title: 2025-07-10 Novus Pharma - Onprem / Air-gapped Deployment Discovery

Redwood AE/SE to provide on‑prem checklist, security pack, and estimated sizing/pricing. Next step: schedule deep dive with infra and procurement; run pilot planning call.

transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Okay folks, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood Inference. With me is Priya our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:04] Dr. Alan Cortez: Doing well, thanks. We have a few more minutes blocked, appreciate it.
[00:08] Maya Singh: Hi, Maya here. We’re the security lead. Lots of questions around air-gapped updates.
[00:12] Tom Reed: Tom from IT ops. We'll be responsible for the install.
[00:15] Jordan Lee: Great, high level, Novus is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private on‑prem air‑gapped, right? What’s top priority for you—latency, data residency, compliance?
[00:25] Dr. Alan Cortez: Compliance and data residency are non‑negotiable. We have PHI-ish workflows and need audit trails. Latency is important for some interactive tools but batch is also big.
[00:33] Jordan Lee: Understood. Priya, should I hand over?
[00:36] Priya Nair: Yeah, quick intro to how Redwood handles private deployments—there's a customer-controlled control plane option for private, and then an on‑prem package for air‑gapped environments. We support offline bundle installs and signed images so you can bring them into an isolated network.
[00:50] Maya Singh: When you say signed images, do you have an HSM/KMS integration? We cannot have keys in the cloud.
[00:56] Priya Nair: We do. For on‑prem we support customer-managed KMS and HSM. Typically it's an HSM-backed key for signing. The control plane can be run in your VPC or completely offline; we provide tooling to rotate keys and attest bundles.
[01:10] Tom Reed: How are software updates handled if we're air‑gapped? We can't pull from the internet during install windows.
[01:15] Priya Nair: We provide offline update artifacts—delta bundles you can import. There's an offline update workflow: we produce a signed bundle, you verify signatures using your HSM, then apply. We also provide an update checklist and an install-runbook.
[01:27] Dr. Alan Cortez: How do you handle model updates? Our regulatory team wants to be able to validate model diffs before they go into production.
[01:34] Priya Nair: Good question. For private on‑prem, customers typically have a validated model registry internally. We support bringing model artifacts as part of the offline bundle and we can include checksums, provenance metadata, and a rollout policy that only applies after an approval step. We also integrate with your eval tooling if you want automated regression tests before rollout.
[01:52] Maya Singh: What about model sizes and hardware? We're leaning toward H100s but procurement might push back to A100s to save cost. Any suggestions on performance differences for Redwood runtime?
[02:02] Priya Nair: H100 gives better throughput for large context lengths and for mixed‑precision kernels, but A100 is still supported and can be cost-effective. The runtime auto-selects kernels and can use quantized variants. We'll provide a recommended profile—batch sizes, sequence lengths, and quantization profiles—based on your typical workloads.
[02:19] Jordan Lee: We should capture examples of queries and token rates so Priya can size. Alan, can you share expected QPS and typical prompt lengths?
[02:25] Dr. Alan Cortez: For the clinical notes assistant: peak QPS ~25, avg prompt length ~600 tokens, output ~150 tokens. For research batch evals it's large but tolerant of longer latency.
[02:36] Priya Nair: That helps. For 600 token prompts at 25 QPS, caching and KV cache strategy matter a lot; we'll likely recommend increased KV cache RAM and some batch windowing.
[02:47] Tom Reed: Network topology—will Redwood need egress to your hosted endpoints for telemetry? We only allow outbound to a narrow set.
[02:55] Priya Nair: For air‑gapped, telemetry is optional. We can buffer metrics locally and export them via secure bundle. If you allow limited outbound, we can also ship encrypted metrics to your S3 endpoint in your cloud account.
[03:07] Maya Singh: Audit logs—what level of logs? We need tamper-evident logs for compliance and a way to push to SIEM.
[03:14] Priya Nair: We generate detailed audit logs (token-level traces optional), and the on‑prem control plane can be configured to push logs to your syslog or SIEM. For tamper evidence we support signed log exports and integration with your KMS/HSM.
[03:27] Dr. Alan Cortez: Where does the model catalog live? If we do on‑prem, do we still get Redwood-curated model updates?
[03:33] Jordan Lee: You can opt into Redwood-curated catalog updates but in air‑gapped mode updates are packaged as signed artifacts you import. Alternatively, you manage your own internal model registry and we plug into that.
[03:44] Maya Singh: Licensing and entitlements—how are those enforced without cloud connectivity?
[03:48] Priya Nair: We support license keys that can be validated with an offline entitlement token. We also have node-locked licenses and ID-based licensing that uses signatures. We'll include specifics in the security pack.
[03:59] Tom Reed: Hardware drivers and CUDA versions—do you pin these in the bundle? Our cluster is on RHEL and our ops team is picky.
[04:06] Priya Nair: Bundles include the runtime, recommended container images, and driver compatibility matrix. For air‑gapped installs we provide exact container images and instructions for installing matching drivers. We can support both RHEL and Ubuntu; we'll list supported kernel/module versions.
[04:19] Dr. Alan Cortez: What about fallback plans? If an on‑prem inference node is down, can we failover to dedicated or hosted?
[04:25] Jordan Lee: Yes, we offer routing policies—if you allow outbound connections to Redwood, we can provide automated fallback to dedicated capacity. For strict air‑gapped environments with zero egress, fallback isn't possible, so we'd recommend a multi‑AZ on‑prem setup or extra reserved capacity.
[04:39] Maya Singh: For our security team, we'd like to see SOC 2 Type II and penetration test results.
[04:45] Jordan Lee: Absolutely, we'll include SOC2 reports and recent pen test summaries in the security pack. We'll also include our architecture diagrams and a whitepaper on offline update verification.
[04:55] Tom Reed: Estimate timeline—if procurement approves H100s, how long to spin up the first pilot?
[05:00] Priya Nair: Typically 4–6 weeks: procurement and hardware delivery are the big ones, then about 1 week for install and configuration, and 1–2 weeks for pilot validation and smoke tests. If you're using existing hardware, we can be faster.
[05:12] Dr. Alan Cortez: Cost—what does pricing look like for private on‑prem? Is it a flat fee or per-node?
[05:18] Jordan Lee: Private on‑prem is generally a subscription plus node entitlement fees. For Dedicated (hosted reserved) it's monthly reserved capacity. We'll give a more concrete estimate when Priya finishes sizing.
[05:29] Maya Singh: A couple of clarifying Qs: do you support SSO (SAML/Okta) for the control plane admin?
[05:34] Priya Nair: Yes, SAML/Okta and OIDC are supported. RBAC maps to your directory groups.
[05:40] Dr. Alan Cortez: Any limitations on model architectures? Transformers, decoder/encoder?
[05:44] Priya Nair: We support a wide range of transformer-based architectures and provide quantized variants; encoder‑decoder models are supported for seq2seq workloads. We'll confirm specific model support if you have particular models in mind.
[05:56] Tom Reed: For the install window, we need clear rollback steps.
[05:59] Priya Nair: Rollback is supported via image rollback and config snapshots. We'll include a rollback playbook in the runbook.
[06:07] Jordan Lee: Okay, let's recap next steps—Jordan to send security pack and on‑prem checklist, Priya to send sizing and recommended quantization, Novus to confirm hardware preference and share security questionnaire. Any other asks?
[06:20] Dr. Alan Cortez: Could we also get an example offline bundle and a sample verification runbook to show to our auditors?
[06:27] Priya Nair: Yes, we'll provide a sanitized sample bundle and an auditor-friendly verification doc.
[06:33] Maya Singh: Great, thank you.
[06:35] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with those artifacts and propose times for the deep dive.
[06:40] Meeting ends.
